sentences.text: In the year 2022, the respondent no. 4 approached the petitioner company for the purpose of purchasing a vehicle of a particular make.

Initially, the respondent no. 4 deposited an amount of Rs.
4,00,000/- as advance payment.

Later on, on receipt of the entire sale consideration for the vehicle,
the petitioner company delivered the vehicle of choice, made by the respondent no. 4, to him.

In the course of the transactions, an amount of Rs. 26,20,683/- was received from the respondent no. 4 on 05.11.2022 through bank transfer in the petitioner company's current bank account from the bank account of the respondent no. 4.

All the transactions were duly completed between the petitioner company and the respondent no. 4 after receipt of the final part of the sale consideration amounting to Rs. 37,00,000/- from the respondent no. 4 on 04.11.2022.

The sale process of the vehicle was completed with the allotment of permanent vehicle registration number by the Transport Department of Manipur vide Certificate dated 11.01.2023.
2.2.

It was after about 6 [six] months from the completion of the sale process of the said vehicle, the petitioner company came to know that its sole current account had been debit-freezed by the respondent no. 3 Bank authority.
On being approached, the petitioner company was informed by the respondent no. 3 that the account had been debit-freezed on receipt of a notice from the respondent no. 1.
The petitioner company was informed that the same had been done due to some on-going investigation, relatable to the amount of Rs. 26,20,683/-.
But, details of the investigation were not provided.
Page No.# 4/6 2.3.
The petitioner had thereafter, instituted a writ petition, W.P.[C] no. 3191/2023.

It has been stated that when notices were issued to the respondents impleaded therein including the respondent no. 1 herein, the petitioner company was informed by the respondent no. 1 to the effect that the instruction to debit-freeze the current account would be recalled, provided the petitioner company would give adequate security in respect of the amount, which was involved in the then ongoing investigation and the amount in the account would be kept in lien.
As the petitioner company was interested to operate their sole current account, the petitioner company agreed to provide adequate security for the amount of Rs. 26,20,683/-.

In view of the representation received from the respondent no. 1, the petitioner company decided not to proceed with the writ petition and by an order dated 09.06.2023, the writ petition came to be withdrawn.

At the time of withdrawal of the writ petition, the petitioner company was given the impression that the amount of Rs.
26,20,683/- was to be kept on lien on the purported ground that the same was proceeds of crime, as per the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 ['the PML Act, 2002].
2.4.

At the subsequent point of time, the petitioner company collected a copy of the First Information Report [FIR] in connection with which the sole current account of the petitioner came to be debit-freezed.

On going through the contents of the FIR, the petitioner company came to know that the FIR, registered on 03.05.2023, vide Cyber Crime Police Station Rachakonda no. 375/2023 is in connection with offences under Sections 406/419/420, Indian Penal Code r/w Section 66C/66D, Information Technology Act, 2000, as amended.

sentences.text:
With the above projections, the petitioner company has asserted that the sole current account of the petitioner has not been debit-freezed in connection with any offences relatable to the PML Act,
2002.

It is the further contention that the provisions of Section 102, Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 were followed in keeping the sole current account of the petitioner company.
As a result of keeping the account on lien, the petitioner company has to bear substantial cost every month.

It has been contended that as the matter of keeping the account on lien is in violation of the provisions of Section 102, CrPC, the petitioner has preferred the instant writ petition for removal of the lien, put on the account.

4. Issue notice, returnable on 29.01.2024.
5.
The petitioner shall take steps for service of notice upon the respondents by registered post with A/D within 2 [two] working days from today.
6. The petitioner company is carrying its business of automobile dealership within the jurisdiction of this Court and is maintaining its sole current account also within a jurisdiction of the Court.

7. Liberty is granted to the learned counsel for the petitioner to collect the postal receipt number from the Registry and track report may be filed before the Registry prior to the next date of listing.
In view of the projections made above, the petitioner is permitted to collect the copy of notice from the Registry so as to scan and sent it by e-mail to the respondent nos. 1 & 2 along with a downloaded copy of this order and to file an affidavit of service on the next date of listing.
8.

The respondent nos. 1 & 2 are also put to notice to respond as to whether the amount of Rs.
26,20,683/- which has been instructed to be to put on lien is Page No.# 6/6 allegedly proceeds of crime or not in view of the FIR lodged in connection with Cyber Crime Police Station Rachakonda no. 375/2023.
The prayer for interim relief will be considered on the returnable date.
